title: Props, every state
prompt: Paint one sheet of cut-out puppet parts for a paper-puppet film, using the attached image. Panel A is the exact layout, panel B is our footage for these props (reference: copy the object, not the photo style), panel C is the style. STYLE (panel C): flat cards cut from corrugated cardboard, gouache with confident ink linework, the flutes faintly showing through the paint, a thin raw kraft-brown cut edge round every card, brass split-pin brads; shot flat-on, even light, no shadows, no perspective. Copy the craft from C, not the clothes in it. WHAT (panel B): the props of the poem 'Bloodlines', one row each, every state of a prop in its own cell, left to right: the star: a white-gold sphere of light with a soft corona, floating a finger's width above the palms (carried in the parade, handed over, held, rising into the sky, named (label types out), seen through the window well); the name plates: small stamped plates bearing AMOS, IDA, OTIS, RUTH, MAE and the rest; the same plate is the grade stamp on the pine joists (blank, typing, named in the sky, stamped on a joist, glowing above an ancestor beyond the gate); the galaxy: a spiral galaxy held in a thin clear disc rimmed with hammered gold (carried at the hip, raised overhead, turning); the new universe: a clear sphere holding a web of light filaments and nodes that unfolds beyond its rim (born from his hands, held up, nodes blessed, miracle ring); the fingerprint: his fingerprint as concentric ridges, glowing with the ancestors' blood-light, outgrowing the frame (dark, veins arriving from the ancestors' fingers, ridges lighting outward, larger than the frame); the lantern staff: tall carved ebony staff with a brass cage at the top holding a small floating star (raised at the head of the parade, grounded); the mattress pad: thin blue tufted pad, stained, straight on concrete; it does not give (empty, under him). Paint each state as a flat cardboard prop card at the size its cell gives, the same object across its row; a brass brad on the green cross (its pivot); where there is a red cross, that is where a hand grips it. LAYOUT (panel A): paint one card inside each grey ghost, in the same place, size and angle, inside its dashed outline; a brass brad exactly on every green cross; each red cross must fall inside that card's rounded end. NEVER draw a pelvis, hip, shorts or briefs card (the thighs end in a rounded seat that tucks under the hem), a sleeveless vest, lace-up boots, or sunglasses painted onto a head. OUTPUT: only the painted cards on a pure white 2048x1152 sheet laid out as panel A. Leave out panels B and C, the crosses, labels, ruler, dashed lines and ghosts.
